title: Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Fleetwood: Gunners’ Quadruple Dream Goes Up in Smoke
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie SpencerOct 27, 2026Arsenal were beaten from 12 yards by an opponent 84 ranked places lower in the English soccer pyramid. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesArsenal are out of the Carabao Cup after a shock elimination at the hands of EFL League Two’s Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.

The Gunners floundered, failing to get the job done in 90 minutes after initially falling behind and finishing the contest with 10 players following Max Dowman’s first career red card. After ending 1–1 at regular time, they ultimately fell 5–3 in a penalty shootout that decided the fourth-round tie.

The Gunners should have felt a degree of comfort taking to the field at Highbury Stadium on England’s west coast, the venue sharing the name of Arsenal’s beloved home from 1913 until 2006. Fleetwood even play in red jerseys with white sleeves.

The match had to stop only a few minutes after kick off because of a drone being flown above the pitch. But Arsenal were unsurprisingly in control of the ball once the action did resume after the lengthy pause, and the visitors threatened without really putting Fleetwood in serious peril.

Then came the moment every Fleetwood fan dreamed of but probably doubted would become reality. There was nothing remarkable about the buildup, with Harrison Neal knocking the ball forward, and then Aaron Loupalo-Bi just using his strength to hold off 17-year-old Arsenal center back Marli Salmon and unleash a finish beneath stand-in goalkeeper Illan Meslier.

Arsenal never really looked like leveling the game until after halftime, when Martin Ødegaard was introduced and started asking more questions than his teammates had done.

The tide began to change, although there was nothing pretty about the 50th-minute equalizer from Viktor Gyökeres, getting enough on the ball after a cross from teenage debutant Ceadach O’Neill wasn’t dealt with by the Fleetwood defense.

Even then, Arsenal didn’t steamroll their opponent. Kai Havertz missed two excellent chances in the minutes that followed and the early second-half momentum slowed all too easily. Fleetwood looked like they would tire—it’s way more draining to play without possession—but continued to close spaces and fight for every ball.

It was a strong but ultimately fair challenge from Fleetwood’s Neal on Dowman that sparked the 16-year-old’s dismissal with five minutes of the 90 to play. There was no arm around the shoulder from Arteta as the academy gem trudged off the field towards the tunnel, instead receiving what appeared to be a few harsh words from the boss.
Arsenal tried to win it before the shootout, but goalkeeper Jay Lynch made two enormous saves in the final moments.

With no extra time, Fleetwood’s Ronan Coughlan began the shootout by converting with a Bruno Fernandes-esque hop. Ødegaard and Neal traded successes, before Havertz also found the net to make it 2–2 in the tiebreaker. Will Davies wasn’t fazed by the ball appearing to wobble on the spot in the wind, but neither was Gyökeres straight after. Andy Cannon restored Fleetwood’s lead, and then Bruno Guimarães wilted under the pressure, handing over match point. Conor Haughey took it.

Squad depth deserted Mikel Arteta when he needed it most. / Lewis Storey/Getty ImagesThe biggest of dreams is already over by the end of October. Arsenal were targeting an unprecedented quadruple, but where was the depth when it was needed?

Mikel Arteta gave the night off to the Gunners contingent who were at the Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday night. Even without them—Declan Rice, Gabriel, David Raya and the injured Bukayo Saka, it should not have been this hard.
Arsenal still started with seven internationals—with plenty more on the bench, a goalkeeper with 200 Premier League and Championship appearances and a generational teenager.

Fleetwood currently sit 18th in League Two, which makes them the 86th best team out of all 92 members of the Premier League and EFL. Arsenal are reigning English champions and are only off the top of the Premier League on goal difference.

Mikel Arteta’s ideal scenario for this match would have been his team comfortably leading, thereby allowing him to both protect his senior players and hand opportunities to emerging youngsters. In the end, he couldn’t risk using any of the kids on the bench, while none of the three teenagers who started the match finished it. The boss could have done with resting Martin Ødegaard, Ben White, Eberechi Eze, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa but was forced to use all five.
Jurriën Timber did not return for the second half. / Carl Recine/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Illan Meslier—6.2: A slightly surprising choice to start over Kepa Arrizabalaga when he hasn’t played a single competitive match in well over a year. Didn’t get close to a save in the shootout, allowing all five penalties to be scored.

RB: Jurriën Timber—6.5: Captained Arsenal for the first time but only lasted until halftime. He struggled, so it’s hard to say if it was in response to that or pre-planned given how his minutes have also been carefully managed this season.
